title: Generation wire contract
description: The frozen TS<->Python wire contract for automatic plan generation. Definitions only — there is no root type, because the wire carries several independent payloads (a SolveRequest, a GenerationResult, a StageReport). Owned by neither side: the TS types in src/entities/timetable/model/generation/types.ts and the Python dataclasses in the solver package are both projections of THIS document. See ./README.md for the canonical JSON form, the versioning policy, and what is deliberately out of scope. Every object is additionalProperties:false and no property may be null — an absent optional is omitted, never nulled.

Cohort.description: The fixed two-cohort programme structure. Mirrors the DB `cohort` enum (shared/config/cohorts.ts).

WeekMode.description: Course fortnightly eligibility. Mirrors the DB `course_week_mode` enum (shared/config/week.ts).

PlacementWeek.description: Which fortnightly week a placement runs on. Mirrors the DB `placement_week` enum (shared/config/week.ts). An `agnostic` course is always `both`; a `biweekly` course is `a` or `b`.

AvailabilitySeverity.description: Teacher-availability storage severity. Mirrors the DB `availability_severity` enum. `strong` is a hard block. `soft` is a tier-5 objective term, and under the CP-SAT service's shipped clean-mode default additionally a constraint holding tier 5 at its pinned floor — the solve may not add a soft hit the author's own pins did not already own.

Pin.description: An immovable placement inside one cohort (fill-the-gaps: the engine never moves or removes a pin). Exactly four fields — the in-app PlannerPlacement's `id`, `isOptional` and `bundleId` are caller-local markers that never cross the wire, so the projection to this shape happens AT the wire boundary.

WireCourse.description: A course as the engine sees it — opaque ids only. Mirrors GroupingCourse (shared/lib/catalog-hash/types.ts). The PII posture is structural: names, levels, colours and flags have no property here, so additionalProperties:false turns 'the solver only ever sees UUIDs' from a convention into an enforced property of the wire.

AvailabilityCell.description: One plan-scoped teacher-availability cell. `teacherKey` matches a member of WireCourse.teacherKeys (availability is authored per individual teacher).

GeneratorCohortSnapshot.description: One cohort's generation input: its validation catalog, its board as pins, and its parked coverage.

parkedCourseIds.description: One entry per parked (shelved) bundle member — a MULTISET: duplicate count is semantic (each entry covers one required hour), so the canonical sort must never dedupe it.

GeneratorSnapshot.description: The full two-cohort problem snapshot — the engine's only view of the world, and by definition the complete input set of a solve. `snapshot_hash` (generation_jobs) is a SHA-256 over the canonical serialization of exactly this object.

finishesEarlyByCourseId.description: Ids of every course flagged `finishes_early` across BOTH cohorts — a side-set, never a WireCourse field.

GeneratedPlacement.description: One generated course-hour — the engine's output unit, pre-persistence (no ids yet). Unlike Pin it carries its cohort, because the result's placements are a single flat cross-cohort list.

CourseDeficit.description: A course's remaining hours the engine could not place (already net of pins and parked coverage). Only strictly-positive deficits appear.

occupiedSlotsBefore.description: Distinct occupied (day, period) cells before generation (pins only).

occupiedSlotsAfter.description: Distinct occupied cells after merging the generated placements.

lowerBound.description: Provable lower bound on this cohort's occupied slots (max-weight conflict clique, in hours). OPTIONAL and integral: when the engine has no bound the key is OMITTED — `"lowerBound": null` is not a legal wire value.

GenerationDiagnostics.description: CP-SAT is the sole producer on this wire, so its emission semantics ARE the contract: `provenOptimal` is always present, `partial` means exactly `not provenOptimal`, and `stopReason` appears only when the solve did not prove optimality. The in-app TS type stays wider (it still describes the greedy engine, removed in S-309) — the wire is the narrow one.

partial.description: True when the result is not a proven optimum. Identical to `not provenOptimal` — the greedy `signal.aborted` reading is out of contract.

stopReason.description: Why the solve ended, derived from the per-stage `stoppedBy` values: `budget` — a ceiling ended at least one non-optimal stage; `target` — every non-optimal stage stopped at its configured target; `cancelled` — a stop predicate ended a stage (S-305); `interrupted` — the job did not finish (S-304). `stagnation` is deliberately absent: it is a greedy-only reason and greedy never crosses this wire.

GenerationResult.description: What the solver returns: the generated board plus its diagnostics. The 10-tuple `objective` is NOT part of it — that is bench transport (see README, Out of scope).

StageReport.description: One rung of the lexicographic ladder, camelCased for the wire (the solver's internal dataclass and the throwaway .report.json sidecar stay snake_case — see README). In contract because S-303 persists an array of these to generation_jobs.stages. The stage set is VARIABLE-LENGTH and may be sparse: solve_repair emits tiers 1 and 4 only, so never model it as a fixed 10-tuple. `best`/`bound` are per-stage UPPER BOUNDS under `tier_k <= best_k` hardening, not the finished board's objective.

status.description: The raw CP-SAT status string (OPTIMAL | FEASIBLE | INFEASIBLE | UNKNOWN | MODEL_INVALID). Left unenumerated on purpose: it is or-tools' vocabulary, not ours, and it is distinct from the job-level status vocabulary in generation_jobs.

best.description: Objective value at stage end. OMITTED when no solution was found — never null.

bound.description: Best proven bound at stage end. OMITTED when no solution was found — never null.

wallClockS.description: The ONLY non-integer number in this contract. Schema-validated but carrying NO cross-language canonical-byte guarantee (Python renders 2.0 as "2.0", JS as "2"), so a StageReport must never enter a byte-compared or hashed payload. See README, Canonical JSON form / Numbers.

stoppedBy.description: Why this stage ended when it did not prove optimality: `budget` (its ceiling ran out), `target` (it reached its configured target value) or `cancelled` (a stop predicate ended it). OMITTED on OPTIMAL, and on a stage with no solution to attribute — never null.

SolveRequest.description: The envelope the future POST /solve wrapper (F-302) accepts. This is the only place `formatVersion` lives: the snapshot and the result are versioned BY the envelope that carries them, never field-by-field.

warmStart.description: An optional incumbent board to hint the solver with. Same shape as a result's placements.
